japan.rationale: Facts: the Nikkei 225 fell 5.96% to 57,434.77 on Nov 6, entering a bear market (more than 20% below the Jun 22 record), and lost more than 9% on the week, its worst since March 2020. The losses were concentrated in AI hardware imported from the US semis crash (SOX -12.3% on Nov 5): SoftBank -20.8%, Kioxia -36.8%, Advantest -19.6%, Tokyo Electron -13.2% on the week. Topix held up early (+1.2% on Nov 5, when 161-168 of 225 Nikkei names rose on lower oil) but fell about 6% on Nov 6. Interpretation: the shock is mostly US AI beta, not domestic macro (Toyota raised guidance, wages are strongest in about three decades), and Topix/MSCI Japan trackers are less exposed than the Nikkei. It stays -1 rather than 0 because SoftBank reports Nov 10 with CDS near a 4-year high and an OpenAI funding shortfall, and a December BoJ hike to 1.5% is likely while the equity rout continues; the yen near 157.5-158 partly cushions unhedged USD holders.

china.rationale: Facts: Beijing stepped up market support this week (third SFISF swap operation above 100bn yuan on Nov 3, buyback relending rate cut to 1%, permanent buyback lending, PBOC pledge to back Central Huijin, State Council call on Nov 6 to stabilise the stock market). The trade truce looks set to roll forward rather than lapse on Nov 10: Bessent says it runs to January, USTR proposed extending the Section 301 maritime suspension to Jan 9, 2027, the US paused a blacklist rule, and Xi and Trump meet at APEC Shenzhen on Nov 18-19; MOFCOM has not published a rare-earth extension. Offsets: October NBS PMI 49.3, CSI 300 in a bear market, retail participation at one-year lows, and HK tech fell with the US $2.3tr tech plunge on Nov 6 after rallying on Nov 5. Interpretation: a policy put plus a lower trade-tail risk tilt the 1-3 month view mildly positive, but the rally is beta to US AI sentiment and binary on the summit and the Tencent (Nov 18) / Alibaba (Nov 19) prints, hence low confidence; downgrade to 0 if the summit slips or Beijing lets the rare-earth suspension lapse.

regime_notes: One AI-buildout shock dominated: the post-midterm data-centre backlash and the Microsoft/Oracle/neocloud pullback drove SOX -12% on Nov 5, and Japan's AI-hardware names (SoftBank, Advantest, TEL, Kioxia) took the hit as high-beta proxies, pushing the Nikkei into a bear market. Japan's damage is index-specific: the price-weighted Nikkei fell far more than Topix/MSCI Japan, and domestic and real-estate names gained on lower oil. China/HK is not a hedge against that factor: HK tech rallied on Nov 5 and then fell with the US on Nov 6, while policy support (swap facility, relending cut, State Council) limits drawdowns without driving a durable rally. The trade truce appears to be rolling forward (USTR maritime-301 proposal to Jan 9, 2027; Xi-Trump at APEC Shenzhen Nov 18-19), but MOFCOM has not confirmed the rare-earth suspension beyond Nov 10. Nov 10 (SoftBank results, TSMC October sales, US CPI, China rare-earth date) and Nov 17-19 (Nvidia, APEC, Tencent, Alibaba) are the decisive dates for both buckets. The BoJ's likely Dec 18 hike to 1.5% supports the yen and banks but adds pressure on a falling equity market.

red_flags.issue: China's suspension of its October 2025 rare-earth export controls legally lapses Nov 10 unless Beijing publishes an extension. US-side signals (Bessent; USTR proposal to extend the Section 301 maritime suspension to 2027-01-09) point to a roll-forward, but no MOFCOM notice was found. Headline risk for China/HK tech ETFs and rare-earth ETFs (MP fell about 15% on the week as the scarcity premium unwound).

Fund-level: KraneShares liquidated seven funds on 2026-10-29, including the KraneShares China Alpha Index ETF and the 2x Long BABA/JD/BIDU/PDD daily ETFs. KWEB and KMLM are not affected; check that no held China product is on the list.

Index choice: Nikkei-225 trackers carry much heavier AI/chip and SoftBank weights than Topix or MSCI Japan trackers; the Nikkei fell more than 9% on the week versus a smaller Topix decline, and SoftBank results (Nov 10, CDS near a 4-year high) are a concentrated single-name risk for Nikkei ETFs.
